note: Numbers the paper states that no committed artifact can produce. Each is an observation from a live session whose raw output was not retained, recorded at the time in a dated findings-log entry or a unit-test docstring written against the live system. They are not measurements from the record and the paper must not present them as such. A record with neither an artifact nor an explicit unretained-session provenance is a build failure, so a number cannot acquire the authority of a derivation by being added here.
why_this_file_exists: This is the paper's own retention thesis arriving a second time. The rule we adopted after the n=210 withdrawal was 'retain per-sample outputs for every study'. It was scoped to studies. These six numbers come from diagnostic sessions against live containers, which are not studies and so were never in scope, and their raw output is gone. Rather than delete the incidents or quietly present them as derived, they are quarantined here with the record that carries them.

hint_chars_repeated.claim: a priority hint of exactly this many characters for two unrelated binaries in one run, and for a third in an earlier session
hint_chars_repeated.record_ref: findings-log.md §3.15 (B6 harness stdout); self-audit-pitfalls.md §'What did catch them'
hint_chars_repeated.note: The later 100-sample run that IS retained (sink_hint_frequency.json) reports 599 min / 2036 median / 2575 max, so 2,575 survives in the record as the distribution's ceiling but the repeat that made it a signal does not.

call_graph_chars.claim: two binaries of different sizes produced call graphs identical to the character
call_graph_chars.record_ref: tests/unit/agents/test_ghidra_program_switch.py docstring ('Measured against the live container on 2026-08-10'); findings-log.md §3.15

call_graph_lines.claim: line count of the same identical call graphs

call_graph_sample_sizes.claim: the two unrelated binaries whose call graphs matched

stuck_graph_chars.claim: the byte-identical call-graph size every sample returned after a failed load left the server on one program

stuck_graph_run.claim: consecutive samples returning that same call graph

unbounded_decode_tokens.claim: tokens generated by one judge call against a documented 8,192-token ceiling that never reached the inference server

unbounded_decode_prompt_tokens.claim: prompt length of that same call

judge_output_cap.claim: the judge model's documented output ceiling, renamed during serialisation to a key the inference server does not read
judge_output_cap.note: Not an observation but a setting, and readable from the source. Registered here rather than derived because a fact builder that reads a settings default would report what the code says rather than what the server received, which is the entire defect.

paged_out_working_set.claim: of the model server's own address space paged out when the host exhausted its swap file
paged_out_working_set.record_ref: eval_sink_hint_ablation.py and analyse_sink_hint_ablation.py module docstrings; findings-log.md §3.26
paged_out_working_set.note: Per-sample host state was not retained. This is the gap §4.5 reports against itself: the retention rule was written about the object under study, and the environment the study runs in is also part of the instrument.

halted_arms.claim: where the first attempt at the paired ablation stopped when the host exhausted its swap file

superseded_rho.claim: the rank correlation the parameter-size series returned before the configuration gate, from five rows that were three models
superseded_rho.record_ref: eval_parameter_size_series.py and test_parameter_size_series_scoring.py docstrings; self-audit-pitfalls.md; findings-log.md §3.34
superseded_rho.note: The current artifact records the refusal, not the superseded correlation, because the gate now stops the series before it computes one. The number survives only in the code that documents why it must not be computed.
